answer: We formulate a mechanism utilizing dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to anchor participants requiring staking collateral and zero-knowledge verifiable delay. Capital barrier analysis proves that layering multiple Sybil identities across this shifting financial dune incurs high slashing penalties, mathematically guaranteeing strictly negative expected attack utility. Thus, these cryptoeconomic security primitives, fortified by copper collateral, force adversarial agents into a robust Nash equilibrium where Sybil multiplication is suboptimal.
